title: SASSA Status: 'Application Complete' — What It Means & What Happens Next
description: Your SASSA application has been submitted successfully. Learn what this status means, how long processing takes, and what to do while waiting.
what_it_means: 'Application Complete' means SASSA has received your application and all the information you provided. Your details are now in the queue for verification and processing. This is the first status you will see after submitting your application online or at a SASSA office. It does not mean your application has been approved yet — it simply confirms that the system has accepted your submission.
why_it_happens: You successfully submitted your SRD R370 application on srd.sassa.gov.za
A SASSA officer entered your details during an in-person application
Your application was received outside of normal business hours and is awaiting processing

how_to_fix.title: Wait for Processing
how_to_fix.content: The status will change as your application moves through the verification process. This typically takes a few days.

how_to_fix.title: Keep Your Phone Active
how_to_fix.content: Make sure your registered mobile number is active and has network coverage. SASSA may send you SMS updates.

how_to_fix.title: Check Your Status Regularly
how_to_fix.content: Return to the SRD portal or use the WhatsApp line (082 601 0111) to check for updates.

how_long: The 'Application Complete' status usually lasts 1 to 7 days before changing to 'Pending' or another status as verification begins.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Pending' — What It Means & What To Do
description: 'Pending' is the most common SASSA status. Learn what it means, why it happens, how long it lasts, and when to take action.
what_it_means: 'Pending' means SASSA is actively verifying your information. Your application is being cross-checked against several government databases including the Department of Home Affairs (for identity verification), the South African Revenue Service (SARS) for income checks, the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF), and the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS). Your bank accounts are also being monitored to ensure your income stays below R624. This is a normal part of the process and most applications go through a 'Pending' period.
why_it_happens: SASSA is verifying your ID number with Home Affairs
Your bank accounts are being checked for income deposits
Your details are being cross-referenced with UIF and SARS databases
There is a backlog of applications causing delays
Manual review is required due to a data mismatch

how_to_fix.title: Wait — This is Normal
how_to_fix.content: Pending does not mean rejected. Most applications remain in this status for 1 to 4 weeks.

how_to_fix.title: Do Not Reapply
how_to_fix.content: Applying again while your existing application is pending will not speed up the process and may cause confusion.

how_to_fix.title: Check for SMS Updates
how_to_fix.content: SASSA will send SMS updates when your status changes.

how_to_fix.title: Contact SASSA After 30 Days
how_to_fix.content: If your status remains 'Pending' for more than 30 days, call the SASSA helpline at 0800 60 10 11.

how_long: The 'Pending' status typically lasts 1 to 4 weeks. During peak application periods (the start of each month), it may take longer.

faqs.q: I am pending but the payment window has started — will I still be paid this month?
faqs.a: Possibly, but there is no guarantee. SRD payments run in batches through the last week of the month, and applications are only scheduled for payment once they are approved. If your status is still Pending when batches run, you may be approved later in the window or carried into the following month's cycle.

faqs.q: Is 'Pending' a good or bad sign?
faqs.a: Neither on its own. It is simply the most common status while SASSA cross-checks your details with Home Affairs, SARS, UIF, NSFAS, and the banks. Most applications pass through Pending before a decision is made.

faqs.q: My status has been Pending for months — should I reapply?
faqs.a: No. Reapplying while your application is still in the system can create duplicate records and delay your file further. If Pending has lasted more than 30 days, contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 with your reference number instead.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Bank Details Pending' — How to Fix It Fast
description: 'Bank Details Pending' means your application is approved but SASSA cannot pay you. Learn how to update your banking details immediately.
what_it_means: 'Bank Details Pending' indicates that your application has been approved in principle, but SASSA does not have valid banking information to deposit your grant. Your payment cannot be processed until you provide correct banking details. This is one of the most common reasons for payment delays. The good news is that fixing this is straightforward.
why_it_happens: You did not provide banking details during your application
The bank account details you provided are invalid or incorrect
Your bank account has been closed or frozen
The account name does not match your ID document
You recently changed banks and did not update your details

how_to_fix.title: Log into the SRD Portal
how_to_fix.content: Go to srd.sassa.gov.za and log in using your ID number and registered phone number.

how_to_fix.title: Navigate to Banking Details
how_to_fix.content: Find the 'Update Banking Details' section on the portal.

how_to_fix.title: Enter Correct Details
how_to_fix.content: Provide your full bank name, account number, branch code, and account holder name exactly as it appears on your ID.

how_to_fix.title: Submit and Wait
how_to_fix.content: After submitting, your details will be verified. This usually takes 3 to 7 working days.

how_to_fix.title: Check Your Status
how_to_fix.content: Return to the portal to confirm your status has changed from 'Bank Details Pending'.

how_long: After submitting corrected banking details, verification takes 3 to 7 working days. Payment will be released in the next available batch.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Identity Verification' — What It Means & How to Resolve
description: 'Identity Verification' means SASSA needs to confirm your identity. Learn why this happens and how to complete the verification process.
what_it_means: 'Identity Verification' means that SASSA could not automatically verify your identity through the Department of Home Affairs database. Your application has been flagged for manual identity verification. This may involve submitting additional documents or completing a biometric verification (facial recognition) process. This status is becoming more common in 2026 as SASSA implements stricter security measures.
why_it_happens: Your ID number does not match Home Affairs records
Your name or surname is spelled differently on your application vs your ID document
A nickname or shortened name was used instead of your full name
Your ID document was recently issued and has not propagated to all databases
Your application was flagged for biometric (facial recognition) verification

how_to_fix.title: Check Your Application Details
how_to_fix.content: Log into the SRD portal and verify that your name, surname, and ID number are exactly as they appear on your ID document.

how_to_fix.title: Complete Biometric Verification
how_to_fix.content: If you received an SMS with a biometric verification link, complete the facial recognition process within 72 hours.

how_to_fix.title: Correct Name/Surname
how_to_fix.content: Use the 'Request Names and Surname Update' tool on the SRD website if there is a spelling mismatch.

how_to_fix.title: Visit a SASSA Office
how_to_fix.content: If online methods do not resolve the issue, visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID document.

how_long: Online corrections typically take 3 to 7 working days. Biometric verification is instant once you complete the facial recognition process.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Referred' — What It Means & How to Get Unstuck
description: 'Referred' means your application is being manually reviewed. Learn why this happens, how long it takes, and what you can do.
what_it_means: 'Referred' means your application did not pass the automated checks and has been referred for manual review by a SASSA official. This is not a decline — it simply means a human being needs to look at your application because the system found something that requires human judgment. This status often leads to either approval or decline after the manual review is complete.
why_it_happens: There is a mismatch between your application data and government databases
Your income is borderline relative to the R624 threshold
Your bank account has irregular deposits that need human assessment
Your ID or personal details triggered a manual review flag
There is a potential duplicate application linked to your ID

how_to_fix.title: Wait for the Review
how_to_fix.content: Manual review is conducted by SASSA officials. There is nothing you can do to speed this up.

how_to_fix.title: Do Not Reapply
how_to_fix.content: Reapplying will not help and may create additional confusion.

how_to_fix.title: Check for SMS Updates
how_to_fix.content: SASSA will notify you when the review is complete and your status has changed.

how_to_fix.title: Contact SASSA After 30 Days
how_to_fix.content: If the status remains 'Referred' for more than 30 days, call the helpline to follow up.

how_long: Manual review takes 2 to 6 weeks, depending on the complexity of your case and the current workload at your regional SASSA office.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Means Test Failed' — What It Means & How to Appeal
description: 'Means Test Failed' means SASSA found that your income or assets exceed the allowed limit. Learn what this means and how to appeal.
what_it_means: 'Means Test Failed' means SASSA's checks found income or assets above the limit for the month. For the SRD grant, the income threshold is R624 per month. It is not a permanent ban: you can appeal the specific month within 90 days if you disagree with the information SASSA used. The appeal reassesses the existing record; it is not a route to upload new proof.
why_it_happens: Your bank account received deposits totaling more than R624 in a month
You received a payment from a family member or friend that pushed you over the limit
SASSA detected income from UIF, NSFAS, or another source
You have multiple bank accounts and the combined deposits exceed the threshold
Your spouse's income was included in the assessment for a permanent grant

how_to_fix.title: Check the month and decision date
how_to_fix.content: Open the SRD status portal and confirm the exact month and decision date. The 90-day appeal window runs from that date.

how_to_fix.title: Lodge an appeal if the record is wrong
how_to_fix.content: Go to https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal with your ID number, phone number and PIN. Open the declined month and choose the reason that fits.

how_to_fix.title: Do not rely on new evidence
how_to_fix.content: The SRD appeal rules do not allow evidence that was not available when you applied. Bank statements or affidavits gathered afterwards cannot be added to the SRD appeal.

how_to_fix.title: Correct future assessments
how_to_fix.content: If your bank or contact details are wrong, update them on the SRD portal so later monthly checks use accurate information.

how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise an appeal within 90 days of receiving it. An approved appeal sets aside the decline; payment timing is separate and is not guaranteed by the decision.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Approved but No Pay Day: Next Steps
description: Approved but no Pay Day? SASSA has confirmed you qualify but has not scheduled your payment batch yet. See what it means, how long to wait, and what to do next.
what_it_means: 'Approved but no Pay Day' means SASSA has approved your grant for the month but has not yet scheduled your payment batch. 'Approved' is the status every applicant wants to see. It means SASSA has verified your information and you qualify for the grant. Your application has passed all the checks — identity verification, means test, bank verification, and cross-referencing with other government databases. However, 'Approved' does NOT mean the money is in your account yet. Approved means you qualify; 'Paid' means the money has been released. Between the two, SASSA assigns a 'Pay Day' date that tells you when your payment batch will run. If you see 'Approved' but no Pay Day, your payment is still being processed for disbursement — this is normal for a few days to a week after approval. It does not mean anything is wrong, and it does not mean you will definitely be paid — approval is conditional on your details staying valid until the batch runs. Keep checking your status, and make sure your banking details are correct and your phone is active.
why_it_happens: You met all eligibility criteria for the grant
Your identity was successfully verified with Home Affairs
Your income was below the threshold
Your banking details are valid and verified
You see 'Approved' without a Pay Day because the payment batch for the month has not run yet — approved applications are paid in batches, not all on one day
Your payment is scheduled for the fourth payment day if your grant is under review

how_to_fix.title: Check for a 'Pay Day' Date
how_to_fix.content: Log into the SRD portal and look for a 'Pay Day' date next to your approved status. Approved without a Pay Day simply means your payment batch has not run yet.

how_to_fix.title: Check Again After the 15th
how_to_fix.content: Statuses and Pay Day dates are most reliably updated after the 15th of each month, following bank verification. Check back then before taking any action.

how_to_fix.title: Wait for Your Payment Batch
how_to_fix.content: SRD payments are released in batches over several days. Once a Pay Day date is assigned, it usually takes 1 to 3 business days for the money to reflect in your account. Your neighbours may be paid on a different day.

how_to_fix.title: What If the Payment Date Has Passed?
how_to_fix.content: If the Pay Day date has passed and the money is not in your account, wait 3 business days for the banking system to reflect it. If it still has not arrived, follow the missing grant payment guide step by step before contacting SASSA.

how_to_fix.title: Do Not Close Your Bank Account
how_to_fix.content: Keep your bank account active. Closing it after receiving 'Approved' will delay your payment, and your details must match your ID exactly.

how_to_fix.title: Check Payment Method
how_to_fix.content: Confirm whether payment will be made to your bank account, Postbank, or retail collection point. For retail collection, wait for the payment SMS before going to the store.

how_long: After 'Approved', a Pay Day date is usually assigned within 1 to 7 days. Payment usually reflects within 1 to 3 business days after the Pay Day date. If your grant is under review, you will be paid on the fourth payment day once SASSA confirms the date.
what_not_to_do: Do not reapply — a new application will not speed up your Pay Day and can delay your existing file.
Do not pay anyone to 'release' or 'speed up' your payment. SASSA never charges a fee.
Do not close or change your bank account while you are waiting for the batch to run.
Do not share your OTP, PIN, or password with anyone who contacts you claiming to be from SASSA.
Do not travel to a retail collection point until you have received the payment SMS with your collection code.

faqs.q: What does 'Approved but no Pay Day' mean?
faqs.a: It means your application is approved, but a Pay Day has not been shown yet. In other words, SASSA has verified that you qualify for the month, but your payment has not yet been assigned to a payment batch. A Pay Day date is usually added within a few days to a week after approval.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Approved with a Pay Day and Approved without one?
faqs.a: 'Approved' means you qualify for the month. A 'Pay Day' date means SASSA has scheduled your payment batch for a specific day. If you see Approved with no Pay Day, your payment simply has not been scheduled yet — it does not mean anything is wrong with your application.

faqs.q: How long after 'Approved' until I get a Pay Day?
faqs.a: There is no officially published timeframe, but in practice a Pay Day is usually assigned within a few days to a week after approval. Statuses and Pay Day dates are most reliably updated after the 15th of each month, following bank verification. If no Pay Day appears for more than 3 weeks, contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11.

faqs.q: Should I reapply if I am approved but have no Pay Day?
faqs.a: No. Reapplying will not create a Pay Day faster and may cause problems with your existing application. Keep checking your status on the official SRD portal instead.

faqs.q: Is 'Approved but no Pay Day' the same as 'Pending'?
faqs.a: No. 'Pending' means SASSA is still verifying whether you qualify at all. 'Approved without a Pay Day' means verification is complete and you qualify — only the payment scheduling step remains. Approval is the stronger status of the two.

faqs.q: I was approved but received no SMS — what now?
faqs.a: SMS notifications depend on your registered number being active and can be delayed or undelivered. Your status on the official portal is the reliable source of truth, so check it directly at srd.sassa.gov.za. Make sure your phone number is correct and your inbox is not full.

faqs.q: Can I be approved and then never paid?
faqs.a: Approval is assessed monthly and remains subject to your details staying valid until the payment batch runs. If your banking details become invalid, your income exceeds the threshold, or a new database check flags your application, your status can change before payment. That is why it is important to keep your bank details and phone number up to date.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA 'Declined': What It Means and How to Appeal
description: A declined SRD status means SASSA did not approve that month. See what to check, how to appeal within 90 days, and what the tribunal can reassess.
what_it_means: 'Declined' means SASSA did not approve your SRD application for that month. Each month is assessed separately, so a decline for one month does not automatically cancel later months. You can appeal the declined month within 90 days of the decision, but the appeal cannot use evidence that was not available to SASSA when you applied.
why_it_happens: Your income exceeded the R624 threshold due to deposits in your bank account
UIF or NSFAS records show you are registered with them
Identity verification failed due to a name or ID mismatch
Alternative income source was detected (gifts, family transfers, informal trade)
You are receiving another social grant
Your banking details are invalid or unverified

how_to_fix.title: Check the decline reason and date
how_to_fix.content: Use the SRD status portal to see the reason shown for that month and the date of the decision. The 90-day appeal window runs from that date.

how_to_fix.title: Lodge an appeal within 90 days
how_to_fix.content: Go to https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal with your 13-digit ID number, the 10-digit phone number on your application and the 6-digit PIN. Open the declined month and choose the appeal reason that fits.

how_to_fix.title: Use only information SASSA already had
how_to_fix.content: The tribunal reassesses the decision on the information available at application. You cannot add new bank statements, affidavits or other evidence at the appeal stage.

how_to_fix.title: Fix the root cause for future months
how_to_fix.content: If the decline came from outdated bank or contact details, correct them on the SRD portal so later monthly assessments use accurate information.

how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise an appeal within 90 days of receiving it. If the appeal is declined, you can apply again for a later month if you still qualify.

faqs.q: I was approved last month but declined this month — why?
faqs.a: The SRD grant is reassessed every single month. A change between months — such as a bank deposit that pushed you over the R624 threshold, an UIF or NSFAS record appearing against your ID, or a verification mismatch — can cause a decline for that specific month even if you were approved before. Check your decline reason on the portal to see which check failed.

faqs.q: Can I be approved again in a future month?
faqs.a: Yes. Each month is assessed separately. If the issue that caused the decline no longer applies — for example your bank balance drops back under the threshold — you can be approved again in a later cycle without reapplying.

faqs.q: Does one decline mean my application is cancelled?
faqs.a: No. A decline applies only to the month in question. Your application stays in the system and is reassessed for each new month.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA 'Appeal Pending': What It Means & Next Steps
description: 'Appeal Pending' means an SRD appeal has been lodged for a declined month and no tribunal decision is recorded yet. Check it with your ID, phone and PIN.
what_it_means: 'Appeal Pending' means an appeal has been lodged for a declined SRD month and the Independent Tribunal has not yet recorded a decision. It is not an approval, and it is not a second decline. The tribunal must finalise the appeal within 90 days of receiving it.
why_it_happens: You lodged an appeal for that month on the official SASSA SRD appeals portal
The appeal is linked to your ID number and the month, not to a separate reference number
The Independent Tribunal is reassessing SASSA's decision on the information already available
The tribunal has not yet communicated a decision for that month

how_to_fix.title: Check the month, not an overall status
how_to_fix.content: The appeals portal records outcomes per month. Open the specific month you appealed instead of looking for one overall appeal status.

how_to_fix.title: Check with your ID, phone and PIN
how_to_fix.content: Go to https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal, enter your 13-digit ID number and the 10-digit phone number on your SRD application, then enter the 6-digit PIN sent to that phone.

how_to_fix.title: Wait for the 90-day tribunal period
how_to_fix.content: The tribunal must finalise the appeal within 90 days of receiving it. Pending during that period does not mean the appeal failed.

how_to_fix.title: Do not lodge a duplicate for the same month
how_to_fix.content: The portal rejects a second appeal for the same period. If your circumstances change, submit a new SRD application for a later month.

how_to_fix.title: Keep your phone number active
how_to_fix.content: The PIN and the decision are sent to the phone number on your SRD application. If that number changes, update it on the SRD portal.

how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise the appeal within 90 days from the date it receives the appeal. If that period passes with no outcome, follow up through official SASSA channels.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Paid' — What It Means & What to Do If Money Is Not Received
description: 'Paid' means SASSA has released your payment. Learn what to do if the money has not reached your account and how to track your payment.
what_it_means: 'Paid' is the final and best status — it means SASSA has successfully processed your payment and the funds have been released. However, 'Paid' does not mean the money is already in your account. Depending on your bank, it can take 1 to 3 business days for the payment to reflect. This delay is normal and is caused by the banking system processing times, not SASSA.
why_it_happens: Your grant was approved and a Pay Day date was assigned
SASSA processed the payment batch and sent it to the bank
The payment was sent via your chosen payment method (bank transfer, Postbank, or retail)

how_to_fix.title: Wait 1 to 3 Business Days
how_to_fix.content: Bank processing times vary. The money may not appear immediately even though the status says 'Paid'.

how_to_fix.title: Check Your Bank Account
how_to_fix.content: Log into your banking app or check your balance at an ATM.

how_to_fix.title: Check for an SMS
how_to_fix.content: If you collect at retail (Pick n Pay, Boxer), wait for the SMS collection code before going to the store.

how_to_fix.title: Contact SASSA After 5 Days
how_to_fix.content: If the money has not reflected after 5 business days, call the SASSA helpline at 0800 60 10 11.

how_long: Once 'Paid' is shown, money usually reflects within 1 to 3 business days. Retail collection SMS may take 1 to 2 days.
what_not_to_do: Do not go to a retail collection point without the payment SMS — staff cannot release funds without the collection code.
Do not reapply or submit a new application because a payment has not reflected yet.
Do not pay anyone who offers to 'trace' your money for a fee. SASSA never charges for payment queries.

faqs.q: My Pay Day is today but I have not received my money — why?
faqs.a: Pay Day is the day SASSA releases your payment batch, not the moment cash reaches your account. Bank transfers usually reflect within 1 to 3 business days after Pay Day, depending on your bank. If you collect at a retail point, wait for the payment SMS with your collection code before going to the store.

faqs.q: My status says 'Paid' but there is no money after 3 days — what should I do?
faqs.a: First confirm which payment method is on your profile (bank account, Postbank, or retail collection) and check that account directly. If nothing has reflected after about 5 business days, follow our missing grant payment guide step by step, then contact SASSA on 0800 60 10 11 with your reference number.

faqs.q: How do I know if my Pay Day has passed or moved?
faqs.a: Check your status on the official SRD portal. If a Pay Day date is still shown, wait the full 1 to 3 business days for bank reflection. If the date has disappeared or changed, your payment may have been reassigned to another batch — check again after the 15th of the month and contact SASSA if it stays unresolved.

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Under Review' — What It Means & What Happens Next
description: Under Review means SASSA is re-examining your application before a final decision. Learn why this happens, how long it takes, and what to do.
what_it_means: 'Under Review' means SASSA is actively re-examining your application before making a final decision. This is similar to 'Referred' but is often shown when your application has already been provisionally assessed and is being double-checked — for example after an appeal, a banking detail change, or a data mismatch. It is not a decline, and it is not a cancellation. It simply means your file is being checked again by the system or by a SASSA official before a Pay Day is assigned or a decision is confirmed. This status is also used during SASSA's 2026/27 grant-review programme. If you received an SMS or letter asking you to visit a SASSA office, your grant will show as 'Under Review' while that check is outstanding. You have up to 90 days from the notice to present yourself — an initial 30 days to submit the requested information, and a further 60 days before the grant may be suspended. A review is an administrative control to confirm you still qualify — it is not a cancellation. See our full grant review guide for step-by-step help.
why_it_happens: Your application was flagged for a second check after a banking detail change or status update
You recently lodged an appeal and SASSA is re-evaluating your case
A data mismatch between your application and a government database triggered a manual review
Your grant is being verified for the new month's payment cycle
You received a grant review notice and have not yet presented yourself at a SASSA office

how_to_fix.title: Wait for the Review to Complete
how_to_fix.content: There is nothing you can do to speed up the review. Most reviews complete within 2 to 4 weeks.

how_to_fix.title: Do Not Reapply
how_to_fix.content: Reapplying while your application is under review creates duplicate records and can delay the process.

how_to_fix.title: Check Your Status After the 15th
how_to_fix.content: Statuses are most reliably updated after the middle of the month. Check back then before taking action.

how_to_fix.title: Contact SASSA After 30 Days
how_to_fix.content: If the status stays Under Review for more than 30 days, call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11.

how_to_fix.title: Received a Review Notice? Attend Within 90 Days
how_to_fix.content: If SASSA sent you an SMS or letter to attend a grant review, do not ignore it. SASSA allows up to 90 days from the notice: an initial 30 days to submit the requested information, and a further 60 days before the grant may be suspended. Bring your ID and the documents SASSA asked for. A review is not a cancellation — if you still qualify, your grant continues.

how_long: 'Under Review' typically lasts 2 to 4 weeks, but can take longer if the review is complex or if there is a backlog.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Cancelled' — What It Means & How to Get Your Grant Back
description: 'Cancelled' means your SASSA grant was cancelled. Learn the common reasons and the exact steps to reinstate or reapply.
what_it_means: 'Cancelled' means SASSA has removed your grant from the payment system. This is different from a monthly decline — a cancellation means your entire application has been closed or withdrawn. The most common reason is not collecting your grant for three consecutive months, which causes SASSA to suspend and eventually cancel the application. A cancellation is not a permanent ban. You can reapply at any time on the official SRD portal with your ID number, and your reapplication is assessed on the same monthly cycle as new applications.
why_it_happens: You did not collect your grant for three consecutive months
Your application was flagged during verification and then cancelled
You no longer meet the eligibility criteria
SASSA found duplicate or fraudulent activity on your file

how_to_fix.title: Reapply on the SRD Portal
how_to_fix.content: Go to srd.sassa.gov.za and submit a new application with your 13-digit ID number. It is free and takes a few minutes.

how_to_fix.title: Reapply via WhatsApp or Moya
how_to_fix.content: You can also reapply through the SASSA WhatsApp line (082 601 0111) or the Moya app (zero data).

how_to_fix.title: Check Whether a Month Was Declined
how_to_fix.content: A cancellation is not the same as a declined month, so check the portal for a specific decline reason and date. If a month was declined, you can appeal that month within 90 days. If there is no declined month, reapply instead of lodging an appeal.

how_long: A reapplication is assessed on the same monthly cycle as new applications. Check your status after the 15th of the month.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Suspended' — What It Means & How to Reinstate
description: 'Suspended' means your SASSA grant has been temporarily halted. Learn why grants get suspended and the exact steps to get yours reinstated.
what_it_means: 'Suspended' means your grant payments have been temporarily halted. A suspension is the step that comes before cancellation. It most commonly happens after you do not collect your grant for three consecutive months, and it is also used during SASSA's 2026/27 grant-review programme when a beneficiary has not responded to a review notice. A grant is suspended after the review response period (an initial 30 days to submit information, plus a further 60 days) has passed without a response. Unlike a cancellation, a suspension may be reversible by attending the outstanding review: if SASSA confirms you still qualify, the suspension is lifted and you are back-paid for the suspended period. Once suspended, apply for restoration within 30 days of the suspension before the grant can be lapsed. See our full grant review guide for step-by-step help.
why_it_happens: You did not collect your grant for three consecutive months
You did not respond to a grant review notice within 90 days
SASSA flagged your application for additional verification
Your banking details became invalid and were not updated
A system review paused your payment while checks ran

how_to_fix.title: Contact SASSA
how_to_fix.content: Call the SASSA helpline on 0800 60 10 11 to ask why your grant was suspended and how to reinstate it.

how_to_fix.title: Reapply If Needed
how_to_fix.content: If your grant was suspended because you stopped collecting, you may need to reapply on the SRD portal with your ID number.

how_to_fix.title: Update Your Details
how_to_fix.content: Make sure your banking details and phone number are correct before reapplying.

how_to_fix.title: Attend Your Grant Review
how_to_fix.content: If the suspension followed a missed grant review, visit your nearest SASSA office with your ID and documents to complete the review. If you still qualify, the grant is reinstated and you are back-paid for the suspended period. Apply for restoration within 30 days of the suspension — after that the grant can be lapsed.

how_long: Processing a reinstatement or reapplication can take up to a full monthly cycle. Check your status after the 15th.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Reapplication Required' — What It Means & How to Reapply
description: 'Reapplication Required' means SASSA needs you to submit a fresh application. Learn why this happens and how to reapply fast and free.
what_it_means: 'Reapplication Required' means SASSA needs you to submit a brand new application to continue receiving your grant. This usually happens when your previous application was cancelled, lapsed, or suspended and SASSA no longer has an active application on file. It is not a rejection of your eligibility — it simply means you need to re-apply. Reapplying is free and takes a few minutes.
why_it_happens: Your previous grant was cancelled after you stopped collecting for three months
Your application lapsed and was not renewed
SASSA requires a fresh application for a new payment cycle
Your prior application was incomplete and SASSA closed it

how_to_fix.title: Go to the SRD Portal
how_to_fix.content: Visit srd.sassa.gov.za and submit a new application with your 13-digit ID number.

how_to_fix.title: Reapply via WhatsApp or Moya
how_to_fix.content: You can reapply through the SASSA WhatsApp line (082 601 0111) or the Moya app (zero data).

how_to_fix.title: Check Your Status After the 15th
how_to_fix.content: Reapplications are assessed on the same monthly cycle as new applications. Check your status after the middle of the month.

how_long: A reapplication is assessed on the same monthly cycle as new applications — usually within the current or next payment window.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Alternative Income Detected' — What It Means & How to Appeal
description: 'Alternative Income Detected' means SASSA identified income from another source. Learn what counts as income and how to appeal this decline.
what_it_means: 'Alternative Income Detected' means SASSA's checks found another income source for that month. The check can use bank and government records, and a family transfer, once-off deposit or old record can trigger it. It does not automatically prove you earned a salary, but SASSA did not accept that you met the income test for that month. You can appeal the month if the record is wrong, but you cannot add new evidence at the appeal stage.
why_it_happens: A family member sent you money via e-wallet or bank transfer
A stokvel payout was deposited into your account
You received a UIF payment or NSFAS stipend
Someone used your bank account for their own transactions
You do informal work that pays irregularly into your account

how_to_fix.title: Check the exact month and reason
how_to_fix.content: Use the SRD status portal to confirm the month, the decline reason and the decision date. Each month has its own 90-day appeal window.

how_to_fix.title: Lodge the appeal on the official portal
how_to_fix.content: Go to https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal, enter your ID and phone number, then the 6-digit PIN. Open the declined month and choose no_alternative_income_source if it fits.

how_to_fix.title: Understand the evidence limit
how_to_fix.content: The tribunal reassesses the information SASSA already had. The SRD appeal form is a reason selection, not a document-upload form, and new bank statements or affidavits cannot be added.

how_to_fix.title: Fix future months
how_to_fix.content: Correct wrong bank or contact details on the SRD portal for future assessments. A correction does not change the month you are appealing.

how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise the appeal within 90 days of receiving it. A declined appeal confirms the decision for that month; you can apply again for a later month if you qualify.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'UIF Registered' — What It Means & How to Fix It
description: 'UIF Registered' means SASSA found you on the Unemployment Insurance Fund database. Learn why this blocks your grant and how to resolve it.
what_it_means: 'UIF Registered' means SASSA cross-checked your ID number against the Department of Employment and Labour's UIF database and found that you appear as a registered contributor or recipient. Even if you are not currently receiving UIF payments, simply being registered can trigger this status and block your SRD grant. This often happens because a former employer never deregistered you when you left.
why_it_happens: Your previous employer did not deregister you from UIF when you left
You applied for and received UIF payments during the assessment period
Your employer is still contributing to UIF on your behalf
There is an old UIF claim on your ID from a previous job

how_to_fix.title: Check your UIF record
how_to_fix.content: Contact the Department of Employment and Labour or your nearest Labour Centre to confirm whether the UIF record is active and accurate.

how_to_fix.title: Ask for deregistration for future months
how_to_fix.content: Ask your former employer or the Labour Centre to correct the record. This helps future SRD assessments but does not add evidence to an appeal for a past month.

how_to_fix.title: Appeal the declined month if the record was wrong
how_to_fix.content: Lodge on https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal within 90 days of the decision and choose the UIF-related reason shown. The appeal reassesses the record SASSA had; you cannot upload a new clearance letter at this stage.

how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise an appeal within 90 days of receiving it. Fixing the UIF record is a separate process and depends on your former employer and the Labour Centre.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'NSFAS Registered' — What It Means & How to Fix It
description: 'NSFAS Registered' means SASSA found you on the National Student Financial Aid Scheme database. Learn how to prove you are no longer a student.
what_it_means: 'NSFAS Registered' means SASSA checked your ID number against the National Student Financial Aid Scheme (NSFAS) database and found that you appear as an active beneficiary. This blocks your SRD grant because student funding counts as alternative income. It often happens to students who graduated or dropped out but were never removed from the NSFAS system.
why_it_happens: You graduated but your university did not update your status with NSFAS
You dropped out but NSFAS still shows you as active
You applied for NSFAS but never received funding
A data error links your ID to another person's NSFAS record

how_to_fix.title: Check your NSFAS record
how_to_fix.content: Contact your university financial aid office or NSFAS to confirm whether the record still shows you as an active beneficiary.

how_to_fix.title: Ask for the record to be corrected
how_to_fix.content: Request a correction if you graduated, dropped out or never received funding. This helps future assessments but is not new evidence for a past appeal.

how_to_fix.title: Appeal the declined month if the record was wrong
how_to_fix.content: Lodge on https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal within 90 days and choose the NSFAS-related reason shown. The tribunal reassesses the information SASSA had; there is no document upload in the SRD appeal form.

how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise an appeal within 90 days of receiving it. Correcting the NSFAS record is a separate process.

who_to_contact.label: University financial aid office or NSFAS

author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Source Limit Exceeded' — What It Means & How to Appeal
description: 'Source Limit Exceeded' means your total deposits across all sources went over the allowed limit. Learn what triggers this and how to appeal.
what_it_means: 'Source Limit Exceeded' means the total money SASSA counted from all sources for that month went over the R624 limit. It is related to 'Alternative Income Detected' and 'Means Test Failed'. You can appeal the month if the record is wrong, but the appeal reassesses the existing information and does not allow new evidence.
why_it_happens: Multiple deposits from different sources pushed your total over the limit
A large one-off deposit from a family member or refund was counted
You receive income on top of a gift or stokvel payout
You have multiple bank accounts and the combined deposits exceed the threshold

how_to_fix.title: Check the month and decision date
how_to_fix.content: Confirm the exact month and decision date on the SRD status portal. The 90-day appeal window runs from that date.

how_to_fix.title: Lodge the appeal if you disagree
how_to_fix.content: Go to https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal, verify with your ID, phone and PIN, open the declined month and choose the reason that fits.

how_to_fix.title: Do not rely on uploading statements
how_to_fix.content: The SRD appeal form does not provide a document upload and the rules do not allow information that was not available at application.

how_to_fix.title: Reduce future flags
how_to_fix.content: Keep the account used for SRD separate and avoid unnecessary large transfers into it before future monthly checks.

how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise an appeal within 90 days of receiving it. There is no guarantee of back pay from the appeal decision alone.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Application Invalid' — What It Means & How to Fix It
description: 'Application Invalid' means your application was missing required or correct information. Learn how to fix it and get your grant back on track.
what_it_means: 'Application Invalid' means your SASSA application could not be processed because the information you provided was missing, incorrect, or did not match the required format. This is different from a decline based on eligibility — it means the application itself failed validation. The most common causes are an incorrect ID number, a wrong or inactive phone number, or missing banking details.
why_it_happens: Your 13-digit ID number was entered with a typo
The phone number you provided is not registered in your name (not RICA'd)
Your banking details are missing or incorrect
Required fields were left blank during application

how_to_fix.title: Check Your Details
how_to_fix.content: Log into the SRD portal and verify your ID number, phone number, and banking details are correct.

how_to_fix.title: Submit a New Application
how_to_fix.content: If the application cannot be corrected, submit a fresh application with the correct details on srd.sassa.gov.za.

how_to_fix.title: Use a RICA'd Number
how_to_fix.content: Make sure your phone number is registered in your name so SASSA can send OTPs and updates.

how_long: A corrected or new application is processed on the same monthly cycle. Check your status after the 15th.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Null' or No Status — What It Means & What to Do
description: A 'Null' or empty SASSA status means no status is showing for your application. Learn why this happens and how to get your status to appear.
what_it_means: A 'Null' or blank status means the SRD system is not showing any status for your application. This is usually a temporary data issue that happens when a new application has just been submitted, when there is a system backlog, or when your details did not fully sync. It does not mean your application was rejected. In most cases the status appears within 24 to 48 hours once the system processes your details.
why_it_happens: You just applied and the system has not processed your details yet
There is a backlog of applications causing a delay
Your application data did not fully load or sync
The SRD portal is experiencing temporary technical issues

how_to_fix.title: Wait 24 to 48 Hours
how_to_fix.content: A Null status right after applying is normal. Wait a day or two and check again.

how_to_fix.title: Clear Your Browser or App Cache
how_to_fix.content: Try a fresh browser session or update the Moya app and check again.

how_to_fix.title: Try Another Method
how_to_fix.content: Check via USSD (*120*69277#), WhatsApp, or call the SASSA helpline instead of the portal.

how_to_fix.title: Contact SASSA If It Persists
how_to_fix.content: If the status stays blank for more than a few days, call 0800 60 10 11.

how_long: A Null status usually resolves within 24 to 48 hours. If it persists beyond a few days, contact SASSA.
author: Lucky Cungwa

title: SASSA Status: 'Self-Exclusion Response Found' — What It Means & How to Fix It
description: 'Self-Exclusion Response Found' is a generic SRD decline message. The system found a disqualifying factor but does not say which one. Learn the likely causes and how to pin down and fix yours.
what_it_means: 'Self-Exclusion Response Found' comes from SASSA's automated means test. Each month the system cross-checks your ID against databases - UIF, NSFAS, SARS, the government payroll (PERSAL), the CIPC company register, your bank accounts - and when one of those checks finds something, it can report a generic 'self-exclusion response' instead of naming the exact source. Despite the name, it usually does not mean you excluded yourself. It means the system found a reason it believes you do not qualify, but it has not shown you which one. Your job is to identify the underlying check that failed.
why_it_happens: The UIF database shows your ID as employed or receiving UIF benefits - often a stale registration a previous employer never closed
NSFAS lists you as an active funded student
Your ID appears on the government payroll (PERSAL), even for a contract that ended
You are registered at CIPC as a company director
Bank deposits in the assessed month totalled more than {{srd_income_limit}} - including money relatives sent you
You already receive another SASSA grant, which makes you ineligible for SRD

how_to_fix.title: Ask SASSA Which Check Failed
how_to_fix.content: Call 0800 60 10 11 and ask them to look up your application and name the specific reason behind the self-exclusion response. Agents can often see more detail than the portal shows.

how_to_fix.title: Check the Databases Yourself
how_to_fix.content: Confirm your UIF status with the Department of Employment and Labour, check NSFAS for active funding, ask a former employer about a PERSAL record, and search the CIPC register for your name as a director.

how_to_fix.title: Correct the Source for Future Months
how_to_fix.content: Ask the source to correct the record: a stale UIF registration, an ended NSFAS record or a closed PERSAL record. This helps future monthly assessments, but it is not new evidence for an appeal about a past month.

how_to_fix.title: Appeal the Month If the Record Was Wrong
how_to_fix.content: Lodge an appeal at https://srd.sassa.gov.za/appeals/appeal within 90 days of the decision and choose the reason that fits. The tribunal reassesses the information SASSA already had. Letters obtained afterwards cannot be added, and the SRD appeal form has no document upload.

how_to_fix.title: Let the Monthly Cycle Work
how_to_fix.content: Even without an appeal, the grant reassesses monthly. Once the underlying database is corrected, a later month can be approved automatically.

what_not_to_do: Do not reapply just because you see this message - the cause is usually a database flag, and a fresh application will hit the same flag.
Do not appeal without first identifying and fixing the underlying cause; a general appeal without evidence rarely wins.
Do not allow other people to deposit into your SRD account or use it for their transactions.
how_long: The Independent Tribunal must finalise an appeal within 90 days of receiving it. Correcting the underlying UIF, NSFAS or PERSAL record is a separate process, and approval can return in a later monthly assessment.

title: SASSA Status: 'Application Not Found' — What It Means & What to Do
description: A 'Not Found' or 'No Record Found' result usually means the ID and phone number you checked with do not match your application, or no active application exists for you. Here is how to tell the difference and fix it.
what_it_means: 'Application Not Found' (also shown as 'No Record Found') means the SRD system has no active application for the ID number and cellphone number you entered. The most common cause is a phone number mismatch - your whole SRD file is tied to the cellphone number you applied with, so checking with a new or different number returns 'not found' even when your application is intact. It can also mean the application was never submitted successfully, was cancelled, or was deleted in a system reset. It is not the same as 'Declined', which means SASSA assessed you and said no.
why_it_happens: You changed or lost your SIM and checked with a different cellphone number than the one on your application
You entered your ID number incorrectly, or the ID and phone combination does not match any record
The application was never completed or submitted successfully
Your application was cancelled or removed in an administrative reset
You are checking an older month or a different grant system than the one you applied on

how_to_fix.title: Check With the Number You Applied With
how_to_fix.content: Re-enter your 13-digit ID and use the exact cellphone number from your application. If a new SIM is behind this, update your registered number on the SRD portal first, then check again.

how_to_fix.title: Double-Check Your ID Number
how_to_fix.content: One wrong digit returns 'not found' every time. Compare the ID you enter on the portal with the number on your green ID book or smart card.

how_to_fix.title: If It Still Says Not Found, Reapply
how_to_fix.content: If no active record exists and you qualify, submit a fresh application at srd.sassa.gov.za - it takes about ten minutes. There is nothing to lose: a new application is assessed on the normal monthly cycle.

how_to_fix.title: Manage the SIM-Swap Case in Person
how_to_fix.content: If you lost your SIM and cannot receive the OTP to update your number, visit a SASSA office with your original ID to sort out the number on your file.

what_not_to_do: Do not assume you are banned - 'not found' usually means a details mismatch, not a rejection.
Do not keep draining one application system if your number is wrong; fix the phone number on file first.
Do not pay anyone who offers to 'recover' a lost application - applications are free to check and reapply.
how_long: Once you check with the correct ID and registered phone number, your status appears immediately. A fresh application usually shows its first result within 7 to 14 days, and is most reliably read after the 15th of the month.
